speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what are the considerations when selecting (i) primary schools for relocation to new towns and (ii) single-sex schools to become co-ed schools respectively; and (b) how far in advance will such decisions be made known to parents so that they can plan ahead for Primary One admissions for their children.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has plans to relocate schools other than Anglo-Chinese School (Primary) that are currently located in higher income neighbourhoods like Bukit Timah to the HDB heartlands; and (b) what are the Ministry’s consideration in deciding to relocate schools.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has plans to convert more single-sex primary and secondary schools to co-educational schools; and (b) if so, what are the considerations for doing so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In deciding whether or which school to relocate, we are also mindful that each relocation case and its circumstances are unique.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In general, all new schools that MOE opens are co-ed, as is the case of schools opening in recent years in Punggol or those slated to be opened in Tengah.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is to ensure that these new schools meet the local demand for school places for both boys and girls, especially since home-school proximity is an important consideration at the primary school level.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the specific case of ACS (Primary) School, ACS Board of Governors had discussed with MOE on a possible move of one of their two primary schools in the Bukit Timah area to the heartlands to serve a different community and to inject more diversity into their student profile.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE was glad that the ACS Board was open to this request, and subsequently, ACS Board informed MOE that ACS (Primary) School would be the relocating school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As the circumstances for each case are different, MOE takes a customised approach and discusses with key decision-makers in each school to facilitate the transition and provide the necessary support.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I declare that I am on the board of governors of a mission school and the parent of children in an ACS school but not ACS (Primary).

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can I find out what is the Ministry's thinking on single-sex schools and whether the long-term direction of the Ministry is to allow the establishment of more single-sex schools to introduce more options in the education landscape or that we are moving towards more co-ed schools?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, MOE neither have or not have a preference between single-sex or co-ed school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Many of these schools have a history and that is why they are where they are now.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, each case is unique and we will work with the stakeholders accordingly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second point I will make is that I would reiterate what I have said just now.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For every new town, we need to find and create spaces that provide for the local community needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, for example, we will prefer the schools to be co-ed because that would better meet the local community needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Imagine you have three new schools in a new town.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Imagine we have a total of six children – three boys, three girls.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If all the three schools are co-ed, the chances are that each of the school will have 50% boys and girls.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But if one of the schools is not co-ed and it is a single-sex school, then, mathematically, what it means is that the other two remaining schools, chances are that, will have an imbalance between the boys and the girls.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I declare that I am an alumni of ACS but not ACS (Primary), and I am the parent of a student in one of the ACS secondary schools.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Given the shrinking cohorts of students, will more schools in older estates in the future be moved to new estates in this fashion?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And did MOE conduct any consultation with existing and future Tengah residents who are likely to be the parents of future ACS (Primary) students?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, what would happen to the ACS (Junior) site on Winstedt Road after the school moves out in 2039?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that there might have been some recent enhancements done to the campus and would that go to waste when the campus is returned to MOE.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We also have plans to rejuvenate the old towns.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, whether it is a new town or a old town, we will have to look at the current demand and the projected demand in planning for our schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second to the third question – what will happen to the site at Winstedt Road after 2039 – I think the answer is that it will be returned to the state.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: My second question is related to the third question because if there were some enhancements done on the site, then would it be a waste.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Gerald Giam has also brought up a very important point.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In making any decision, we have to consult not just the current generation of stakeholders but also future stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And in any democracy, as I mentioned the other day, one of our biggest challenges is that it may not always be possible for you to consult your future stakeholders because they are not there yet.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because the future residents of Tengah have not even gotten their flats yet and they may or may not know whether they will be residents of Tengah.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, there is where leadership comes in, from both MOE and the ACS board.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have to project not just the needs of the current generation, but also the needs of the future generation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Not just ACS in Tengah but also the broader plans of the siting of the various new schools in the Tengah and Hong Kah area.
